doc.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing Ray Brown on the Oscar Peterson Stratford record
summary: The Oscar Peterson Stratford Festival record with Ray Brown became his Holy Grail; John Eaton introduced him to it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Kind of like Marty Grosz. That style of — © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-

Exactly. Exactly. And then the bass came along, and Ray Brown entered my life with Oscar Peterson at the Stratford Shakespearean Festival, the record I think they recorded in ‘52, and that became the Holy Grail. That became the reason for living was that music for me. I mean it’s amazing how powerful that music was to me. I never heard anything swing that like, I never heard arrangements like that, freedom, joy, everything expressed. Everything that I wanted out of this life was in that record, so I quickly bought it and listened to it thousands of times. I really became so centered on that music that it became really the center of my musical experience. Everything was happening — bop, Charlie Parker, I didn’t care about that.
Can you remember the very first time you heard that recording?

Oh, clearly, clearly. John Eaton, the piano player in Washington who you may or may not know, he’s a wonderful solo pianist, and he does a lot of concerts for the Smithsonian Institute, and he’s a brilliant piano player. He made me aware of this record. And he sat down and he said, “You’ve got to hear this.” I said okay. I sat down and listened to it, and like I said it really —
